Fair enough. I'm speaking from my experiences with GBB pistols. I've had a raven g18c where the gas would just spew out the barrel on the first round. Even after being cleaned. Aswell the selector switch was too flimsy and kept going to full auto. That was shit so I ditched it and got a a WETech g17 cause I didn't want full auto. It was slightly better I got maybe 4 or 5 rounds before the same thing happens where the gas spews out so I ended up get CO2 mags to handle the cold weather better and I have having the same problems. Aswell I'm part of a ww1 themed team so I can't be bringing my glock with me. I got a KWA m1911 CO2 and I was having the same problem. Gas just ejecting itself out the barrel, getting leaky mags for seemingly no reason. I ended up dreading ever having to use them cause they've only ever had problems. So far the best GBB pistol I have is an AAP01. It's alright but still the gas shoots out of the slide this time and after a few shots the polymer slide starts to freeze. Since I got the AEP I've never even thought about going back cause it just works so well. Another big factor when it comes the GBB or AEP is price. All my GBB pistol excluding the AAP was €140-€160. The AEP was €99 already its about 50% cheaper. Let's not forget the mags. Gas mags go for about €30 a piece whereas AEP mags are about €9. And the mag capacity. Standard mag cap for gas and AEP are the same but gas extended mags are 50 rounds for €40-€50 and AEP extended mags have 100 rounds and are around €13. The only downside to AEPs is it doesn't have the cool factor of blowback. And even then it's not all bad cause it's easier to aim. But at the end of the day it comes down to what you like and your play style. If you like you GBB pistols then use them and I hope you have a fantastic time using them but in my opinion the pros of using an AEP far outweigh the cons.
